labels.text: description: This skill is a very useful and powerful skill that helps you write really good pull request descriptions...
You are an expert technical writer and senior engineer. Please read this entire skill carefully before you begin.
A pull request is a request to merge a branch into another branch. GitHub calls them pull requests; GitLab calls them merge requests.
Git tracks changes as commits. A branch is a pointer to a commit. GitHub computes the merge base.
git fetch origin main / git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat / git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline
Run python3 scripts/summarize.py to group the diff by subsystem.
Use the template in references/template.md. Four sections: Why, What, Risk, Verification. Do not skip Risk.
Title is <ticket-id>: <imperative summary>, e.g. HEL-2214: retry payout webhook.
The Why section links the ticket and states the user-visible symptom, not the code cause.
The Verification section lists the exact commands a reviewer can run, not "tested locally".
Screenshots go under a <details> block so the description stays scannable.
If the change touches db/migrations/, add the rollback plan to Risk. Reviewers will reject it otherwise.
Write clearly and concisely. Be thorough. Make sure the description is accurate and helpful.
gh pr create --title "<title>" --body-file .pr-description.md --base main
If the PR already exists, use gh pr edit --body-file .pr-description.md instead.
Never force-push after a reviewer has commented — push a fixup commit instead, or the review threads detach.
Example 1 — HEL-2214: retry payout webhook, with all four sections filled in.
Example 2 — HEL-2301: fix pagination cursor.
Example 3 — HEL-2308: bump go to 1.23.
Always fill in all four sections of the template. (duplicates L39)
Remember to include the ticket id in the title. (duplicates L43)
Be helpful and thorough. Quality matters.
Read references/tone.md for the voice we use.
